newsitem.title: USA: IRAQ NEWS, EXCESS SUPPLY BECALM US FOREIGN CRUDES.
newsitem.headline: IRAQ NEWS, EXCESS SUPPLY BECALM US FOREIGN CRUDES.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude trade was becalmed on Friday by a combination of Iraqi news and excess supply, traders said.
The United Nations on Friday morning gave final approval to Baghdad's pricing formula, setting the stage for the resumption of humanitarian exports once contracts are formally signed.
U.S. refiners continued to mull indications for Iraqi Basrah and Kirkuk grades.

Potential sellers were showing Kirkuk at $1.70-1.80 a barrel under October WTI for mid-September delivery into the U.S. Gulf on a cif basis. Kirkuk hasn't been shipped into the U.S. Gulf since before Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
Basrah was being indicated at $1.90-2.00 under November WTI for early October arrival in the U.S. Gulf.

Both grades are slightly heavier now compared to pre-war measurements. Kirkuk is now assessed at 35.9 degrees API gravity with 1.95 percent sulfur, while Basrah is pegged at 33 to 33.5 API gravity with two percent sulfur, traders said.
On the sweet side of the market, plentiful supplies continued to weigh on prices.

Several companies and trading houses were testing the market for interest in North Sea Brent. End-September to early October delivery of Brent was indicated at 35 cents under WTI, down from around minus 10 cents earlier in the week.
Interest was seen as lackluster as refiners eyed a wide range of other sweet grades on offer.
West African offerings continued to abound, although several of these could quickly evaporate because they were being simultaneously offered into other markets.
A European company, for example, had been showing Bonny Light for September 10-15 arrival in the U.S. Gulf. The crude was recently sold into the Mediterranean instead, traders said.
In Latin America, Colombian Cusiana was offered at around 85 cents under WTI, with bids running far behind at around $1.00 under WTI.
The last deal was transacted last Tuesday at 80 cents under WTI for September 14-18 loading. So far, four cargoes from the September program of 14-15 cargoes have been placed.
One of those sold has been re-sold into the market, while two others were being re-offered, traders said.
Elsewhere in Latin America, Peruvian state oil company Petroperu bought a total of 600,000 barrels of local crude from Block 8 (Lote 8) in its latest purchase tender, traders said.
Petroperu bought the 25-API, low-sulfur crude at an undisclosed discount to West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on an fob basis for August 29-31 arrival.
Block 8 is operated by Argentine Pluspetrol, which holds a 60 percent stake in the field. Korean partners Pedco, Yukong and Daiwoo hold the remaining 40 percent.
Petroperu originally tendered for 380,000 barrels, but ended up buying Pluspetrol's two offers for 400,000 barrels and 200,000 barrels of Block 8 crude.
The crude is destined for use in Peru's Talara refinery.
--Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
